In [[mathematics]], given an [[exterior differential system]] defined on a [[manifold]] ''M'', the '''Cartan&ndash;Kuranishi prolongation theorem''' says that after a finite number of ''prolongations'' the system is either ''in involution'' (admits at least one 'large' integral manifold), or is impossible.

==History==
The theorem is named after [[Élie Cartan]] and [[Masatake Kuranishi]].  Cartan made several attempts in 1946 to prove the result, but it was in 1957 that Kuranishi provided a proof of Cartan's conjecture.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Bryant |first1=Robert L. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Slz1BwAAQBAJ&dq=Cartan%E2%80%93Kuranishi&pg=PA237 |title=Exterior Differential Systems |last2=Chern |first2=S. S. |last3=Gardner |first3=Robert B. |last4=Goldschmidt |first4=Hubert L. |last5=Griffiths |first5=P. A. |date=2013-06-29 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |isbn=978-1-4613-9714-4 |language=en}}</ref>

==Applications==
This theorem is used in infinite-dimensional [[Lie theory]].
